answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid in the auction held at dawn. One bond funds one bidding slot and cannot back another identity while locked. A cipher may hide who controls an account, but it cannot make the same deposit count twice. The market is no free haven for fake identities: running 1,000 eligible agents ties up 100,000 tokens, costing the attacker liquidity and forgone returns.
